readings.role: SEEDED CONTROL — proves the back-edge detector fires on the unbudgeted graph

what_this_supports: The structural half of the operator's capture-budget argument: every cycle must contain a capture, so bounding total captures makes the move graph acyclic, and a DAG has a unique minimax value (no bracket). Measured: 135,494 back edges in the unbudgeted 3x3 graph, 0 with the budget at B=8, at both 3x3 and 4x3. The control firing is what makes the two zeros readable.
what_this_does_NOT_support: Bellman consistency under budget-from-here. That reading was T387's other half and it NEVER RAN — src/t387_budget.zig:717-719 is an infinite loop (bitpos: u6 against a `while (bitpos < 64)` guard its own type cannot falsify; += 1 wraps rather than traps under the -O ReleaseFast tools/runner forces). Proven by sample(1): 2,554/2,554 stack samples at :718-719 after 14h02m elapsed / 836 CPU-minutes / 880 KB RSS / no output file. Do not cite this file as evidence about the Bellman identity. The at-risk class T386 measured is 80/2,748 at 3x3 and 496/51,318 at 4x3; nothing has been compared against those denominators.
follow_up: T397 — promote these readings, fix the loop red-then-green, then take the minimax-identity reading at 3x3 and 4x3 and rule on whether budget-from-here forces the capture counter into the key.
scale_note: The 3x3 budgeted graph is 423,922 states, so a value pass over it is seconds. Any future run exceeding a minute at 3x3 is hung, not slow — a cheap watchdog for the successor.
landmark: No advance. L2 (proven 4x4 values) is unmoved. The row's structural result was already believed and still stands; what changed is that a reading the seat believed was in flight is now known never to have run.
